theory_low.gherib-expressivity-position-argument: Section III F 2, p.14: an informal dimension-count argument, not labelled a theorem and with no stated conditions. The claim needs N >= 2: for N = 1 the N+1 dimensional subspace of R^(2^N) is all of R^2, so nothing is excluded. The quotes and value drop that condition.
theory_low.gherib-expressivity-amplitude-argument: Section III F 2, p.14: an informal argument, valid only when Gaussian overlap is negligible, not labelled a theorem. The claim also needs N >= 2 (the sphere has dimension 2^N - 1, which equals N when N = 1). The value drops the negligible-overlap condition.
theory_low.gherib-sampling-overhead-so2: Section III F 1, p.14: an order-of-magnitude estimate by the authors (|<sigma_z>| about 1e-7 and Nshots about 1e18 for 1% error), not a derivation with stated conditions and not a run. The hardware matrix-element attempt itself failed (Section III B, p.9-10).
theory_low.gherib-norm-conservation-two-vps: Appendix B, p.16-17: a one-sentence design rationale; the only support is that projections are not necessarily norm-preserving. It is not a stated and proved result and the value adds the McLachlan reading beyond the quote.
theory_low.gherib-kramer-saraceno-single-fg-singula: Appendix B, p.17: a short argument. It asserts that the x and p derivatives are orthogonal to the gamma derivative without showing it. It has no theorem label or stated conditions. This is an informal argument, not a proved result.
theory_low.ghosh-re-time-complexity: Section 4.3, p.7 (read from the rendered page): the paper states O(k^(2pi/N)) with k the parameters per LUT gate combination and N the step size, in one sentence with no derivation. A grid search over [-pi, pi] with step N and k parameters would cost about (2pi/N)^k, so the printed form looks to swap base and exponent. Not a proved result.
